Authenticate a user, return a bearer token and set the refresh cookie.

An address with too many recent failures is refused with 429 before the
password is checked. Every failure, whatever the reason, counts against
the address.

Drop the refresh cookie, so the sign-in cannot be renewed.

An access token already issued still works until its expiry, as before:

get.description: Return the authenticated user's identity and consent state.

post.description:
A fresh access token for the holder of the refresh cookie.

The client calls this shortly before its token expires, so a class longer
than the token's lifetime is not interrupted by a sign-in, and on load,
since it keeps the access token in memory only. The account is checked
again, and the sign-in itself still ends max_sign_in_hours after the
password was typed. An access token cannot be refreshed: one taken from
the page ends at its own expiry.

exist in C.L.I.P; see app/services/teams_sso.py.

post.description:
Purge every session past the retention period, and the Teams roster
syncs past it, through the same guarded, batched runner as the daily purge.
Nothing is deleted while a class is running (409), and the run stops between
batches if one starts. A task that fails is reported (503), not hidden.
Cannot be undone, so the body must say `"confirm": true`. The run is audited
with who asked; each batch also audits its counts, as the system. `answers`
is the count taken just before the run.

200.description: One JSON object per line, each with `type` and `request_id`. `accepted` comes first. Then either `delta` events carrying `text`, `citation` events carrying a `citation` (`id`, `material_title`, `source_page`, `source_slide`, `excerpt`, optional `number` and `source_note_id` for discussion notes), `follow_up` events carrying a `prompt`, and `completed`; or one of `unsupported` (with a `reason`), `empty_retrieval` and `error` (with a `detail`).
